hook: LLM systems fail silently — quality decays, costs creep, latency spikes. **You can't fix what you can't see:** traces, cost dashboards, and quality monitoring.

scenes.title: Every call, one trace: **the flight recorder**
scenes.sub: Inputs, outputs, latency, tokens — correlated end to end
scenes.narration: A trace is the full record of one request's journey: the model call with its exact inputs and outputs, latency per stage, token counts, tool invocations with their arguments and results, retrieval details — which chunks, which scores — and the guardrail decisions from GA-23. The properties that matter. CORRELATION: one ID threads user → API → retrieval → model → tools → response — the same discipline as the audit log, now for debugging; the question 'why did THIS user get THAT answer' becomes a lookup, not an archaeology. SAMPLING: at scale you can't trace everything — sample 100 percent of errors and a percentage of successes, and always trace your golden-set questions — the evals' runs must be fully visible. SENSITIVITY: traces contain prompts and outputs — PII-shaped handling — hashed or access-controlled storage, AG-07's rule applied to your own telemetry. A trace you can't afford to keep is a trace you won't have when it matters.

layers.s: User, feature, correlation ID attached at the edge
Query, rewritten forms, top-k chunks, scores, timing
Model, version, prompt hash, tokens, latency, finish reason
Per tool call: name, args, latency, result size, errors

scenes.narration: Notice what per-span detail buys: when a user reports a bad answer, the trace shows WHICH span failed — retrieval surfaced wrong chunks, or generation misread good ones — the same stage-localization as GA-21's metrics, now for single incidents. Finish reasons and error codes deserve their own alerts: a spike in 'length' finishes means context-overflow bugs; 'content_filter' spikes mean something changed in your traffic or your filters; retry-storms show up as duplicate spans. And record the prompt HASH plus version pointer, not just text — 'which prompt version served this request' is a query, matching GA-21's provenance discipline. Instrumentation cost is real — spans add overhead — so make tracing pluggable and standard across services: one instrumentation layer, every pipeline emits the same shape.

scenes.title: Cost dashboards: **spend is a metric, not an invoice**
scenes.sub: Per user, per feature, per model — in near real time
scenes.narration: Token spend is the least-visible production metric — it accumulates in provider invoices, weeks late, with no shape. The dashboard fixes that: aggregate tokens × model pricing into DOLLARS, sliced three ways. Per user/tenant: who spends what — a runaway script, a power user, an abusive trial — each needs a different response, and you can't choose without the slice. Per feature: which PRODUCT capability costs most — the chat feature might cost ten times the summarizer; pricing and architecture decisions need this. Per model and per prompt version: cost shifts when you switch models or prompts — routing more traffic to a cheaper model should show up as a clean delta, not a surprise. Then budgets: alerts at thresholds — daily spend doubles suddenly, page someone; per-request caps enforced at runtime — GA-23's pipeline is where they bite.

items.s: Runaway scripts, power users, abuse — different problems, different responses · quota enforcement
Which capability costs most · pricing and architecture decisions ride on this slice
Daily-spend anomalies page someone · per-request caps enforced in the pipeline

scenes.narration: The cost-quality pairing is the dashboard's real power: plot cost AGAINST quality metrics on the same time axis — a cost drop that coincides with a quality drop is a regression wearing an optimization's costume; a quality rise that costs 40 percent more is a product decision, made with data. Caching effects should be visible too — GA-17's semantic cache shows up as a cost-per-request line stepping down; when the step flattens, cache hit-rate deserves a look. And forecast: monthly run-rate projected from current traffic — the question 'what happens to our bill when this feature 10xes' should have a number attached BEFORE the growth arrives, not after the invoice. Cost observability completes the loop with GA-25's optimization levers — you can only route, cache, and cap what you can measure.

scenes.title: Quality monitoring: **drift shows up before complaints do**
scenes.narration: GA-20 and GA-21 built the offline eval machine; production is where it earns its keep. Three loops. USER FEEDBACK: thumbs, ratings, corrections — cheap, biased, directional — instrument it, read it in aggregate, and treat every thumbs-down as a golden-set candidate: the flagged exchange flows into review, confirmed failures become new eval cases — GA-20's dataset grows from production pain. SHADOW EVALS: sample production traffic — one to five percent — and run the metric stack on it: faithfulness, relevance, retrieval recall — quality trends on REAL questions, continuously, the same delta-alerting discipline as cost: 'faithfulness dropped eight points this week' pages before users write in. DRIFT DETECTION: watch the INPUTS too — question distribution shifts — new topics appearing, language mix changing, query lengths drifting — input drift predicts quality drift, because the system is tuned for yesterday's traffic.

steps.s: User feedback + shadow-eval failures + drift signals
Traces show WHICH span failed · incident or golden-set candidate?
Confirmed failures become eval cases · regression-protected forever
Fix ships only when the eval gate passes (GA-21)

scenes.narration: The loop's cultural meaning: quality becomes a MANAGED quantity — it has a dashboard, a trend line, an owner, and an alert threshold — instead of a vibe reconstructed from support tickets. Two operational notes. Keep the human in the triage step: auto-adding every flagged case to the golden set pollutes it — false positives from user mood, adversarial flags — SME confirmation keeps the gold clean, GA-20's calibration discipline again. And close the loop VISIBLY: when a fix ships from this loop, note it where the team sees it — 'the citation regression users flagged in October is fixed and now regression-tested' — the loop feeds on demonstrated value, and dries up when fixes disappear into the changelog unannounced. Observability, evals, and the fix pipeline are one system — this reel is the connective tissue.

scenes.title: The toolbox: **Langfuse, LangSmith, Azure Monitor** — pick per ecosystem
scenes.sub: And the DIY floor that always works
scenes.narration: The mature options, honestly mapped. LANGFUSE — open-source, self-hostable LLM engineering platform: traces, eval datasets, prompt management, cost tracking; the right default when data must stay in your perimeter or you want hackable internals — generous free tier, real self-hosting. LANGSMITH — LangChain's first-party observability: deepest integration with LangGraph pipelines, first-class dataset and eval workflows; the natural pick when LangGraph is your runtime — commercial, polished. AZURE MONITOR + Application Insights — the enterprise path when you're on Azure: OpenTelemetry-based, fits existing alerting and compliance infrastructure; pairs with MAF's built-in telemetry — AG-15's ecosystem logic. GOOGLE CLOUD and AWS ship equivalents — Vertex and Bedrock observability — same ecosystem-matching rule. And the DIY floor: OpenTelemetry is the standard span format — emit OTLP from your pipeline into ANY backend — the exit hatch that keeps every option above replaceable.

cards.s: Open source · self-hostable · traces + evals + cost · best for perimeter/data-sovereignty needs
First-party for LangGraph · datasets/evals integrated · commercial · best inside that ecosystem
Enterprise Azure path · OpenTelemetry-based · fits existing ops/compliance · pairs with MAF

scenes.narration: Selection heuristics: match the observability tool to your runtime ecosystem — LangGraph plus LangSmith, MAF plus Azure Monitor — because framework-integrated traces are richer than bolted-on ones; choose self-hosting — Langfuse or your own OTLP stack — when data residency or hackability dominates; and whatever you pick, EMIT STANDARD TELEMETRY underneath — OpenTelemetry spans with consistent attribute names — because the tool above should be a replaceable view, not a permanent dependency. Migration reality: teams do switch observability providers; the ones who kept OTel clean switch in days, the ones with proprietary-only instrumentation rewrite. One more practice: keep a 'trace of the week' review — ten minutes, one interesting trace, whole team — observability culture is built by looking, not by dashboards existing.

scenes.title: You can see everything. Now make it fast AND cheap.
scenes.next: Reel 62 · Performance & Cost — caching, routing, fallbacks, quotas

recap: Traces are the flight recorder: correlated IDs, sampled errors fully, PII-shaped storage, span-level detail that localizes failures to retrieval or generation
Cost dashboards slice spend per user/feature/model with delta alerts, runtime caps, and cost-quality pairing on the same time axis
Quality monitoring closes the loop: feedback and shadow evals feed the golden set through SME triage; pick observability per ecosystem with OpenTelemetry underneath

quiz.q: Why must errors be traced at 100% while successes are sampled?
opts: Failures are rarer but carry the diagnostic signal you can't afford to miss; success sampling keeps cost sane
quiz.why: The incidents you need to reconstruct are, by definition, in the error class — sampling them risks losing exactly the evidence you need.

quiz.q: What does pairing cost and quality on one time axis reveal?
opts: Whether a cost change is a genuine optimization or a regression in disguise — and whether quality gains justify their spend
quiz.why: Either metric alone misleads: cheap-and-worse or pricey-and-better are both business decisions that need both axes visible.

quiz.q: Why emit OpenTelemetry even when using a managed observability tool?
opts: It keeps the instrumentation layer standard and portable — switching providers becomes a config change, not a rewrite
quiz.why: The tool above should be a replaceable view of standard telemetry — clean OTel is the exit hatch that keeps the option open.

code.title: Minimal trace decorator — the whole instrumentation habit
code.body:
import time, uuid, functools

def traced(span_name):
    def deco(fn):
        @functools.wraps(fn)
        async def wrapper(*args, **kw):
            span = {
                "trace_id": kw.pop("trace_id", str(uuid.uuid4())),
                "span": span_name,
                "start": time.perf_counter(),
                "model": kw.get("model"), "prompt_hash": h(kw.get("prompt")),
            }
            try:
                result = await fn(*args, **kw)
                span.update(ok=True, tokens=getattr(result, "usage", None))
                return result
            except Exception as e:
                span.update(ok=False, error=str(e)[:200])
                raise
            finally:
                span["ms"] = round((time.perf_counter() - span["start"]) * 1000)
                emitter.send(span)          # OTLP or Langfuse/etc.
        return wrapper
    return deco

# @traced("retrieval") on search · @traced("generation") on complete —
# three decorators and your pipeline is observable end to end.
annot: trace_id threading via kwargs: every span joins the same journey automatically
prompt_hash not prompt text: observability without a PII leak (GA-23 discipline)
finally-block emission: spans fire on errors too — failed calls are the ones you most need to see

notes:
# Observability

## Tracing
- One trace per request: retrieval/generation/tool spans, correlated IDs.
- 100% of errors + sampled successes; golden-set runs always traced.
- PII-shaped storage: hashes, access control, retention.

## Cost dashboards
- Dollars per user/tenant · per feature · per model/prompt version.
- Delta alerts + runtime caps; cost×quality on one axis; forecasting run-rate.

## Quality monitoring
- Feedback → triage (traces localize the span) → SME-confirmed golden cases → gated fixes.
- Shadow evals on sampled traffic; input-drift watch predicts quality drift.

## Tooling
- Langfuse (OSS/self-host) · LangSmith (LangGraph) · Azure Monitor (MAF) — ecosystem match.
- Always emit OpenTelemetry underneath; keep the provider replaceable.
